newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 880,000/bbl of naphtha in May.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 880,000/bbl of naphtha in May.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company, Pertamina has announced the loading schedule for its May allocation of 880,000 barrels of naphtha, traders said on Thursday.
They said the allocated volume of four 220,000-barrel cargoes, is the same as in April.

European major British Petroleum has been allocated two heavy naphtha cargoes from Balikpapan, in Kalimantan lifting May 11-13 and May 20-30 and one full range paraffinic naphtha cargo from Cilacap in Java, lifting May 25-27.
The second Cilacap cargo, lifting May 10-12, will be absorbed domestically by Indonesian petrochemical firm PT Chandra Asri.
Chandra Asri operates a 520,000-tonne-per-year ethylene plant, in Cilegon, West Java.
Traders said some of the cargoes have yet to be sold.
